questions.skill: Compare two treatments with a randomization simulation
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: (Hypothetical simulation results.) Ten plants were randomly assigned to plant food A or B (5 each); mean growth A minus B was 3 cm. In 200 re-randomizations, a difference (A minus B) of 3 or more occurred 4 times. Decision rule: the model is the "no difference" model (plant food does not change growth). Count the simulated results that are differences of 3 or more (A minus B; a one-sided check). If they make up fewer than 5% of the simulated results, the model is not consistent with the data and the difference is significant; otherwise it is consistent and the difference is not significant. Which decision is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: (Hypothetical simulation results.) Ten plants were randomly assigned to plant food A or B (5 each); mean growth A minus B was 3 cm. In 200 re-randomizations, a difference (A minus B) of 3 or more occurred 4 times. Decision rule: the model is the "no difference" model (plant food does not change growth). Count the simulated results that are differences of 3 or more (A minus B; a one-sided check). If they make up fewer than 5% of the simulated results, the model is not consistent with the data and the difference is significant; otherwise it is consistent and the difference is not significant. Which decision is correct?

choices.text: The difference is significant: any difference is significant.
The difference is not significant: it happened 4 times by chance.
The difference is significant: chance gave it only 2% of the time.
The difference is not significant: the groups had only 5 plants.

questions.correct_answer: The difference is significant: chance gave it only 2% of the time.

questions.prompt: (Hypothetical simulation results.) In another plant-food experiment with random assignment, mean growth A minus B was 1.2 cm. In 200 re-randomizations, differences (A minus B) of 1.2 or more occurred 62 times. Decision rule: the model is the "no difference" model (plant food does not change growth). Count the simulated results that are differences of 1.2 or more (A minus B; a one-sided check). If they make up fewer than 5% of the simulated results, the model is not consistent with the data and the difference is significant; otherwise it is consistent and the difference is not significant. Which decision is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: (Hypothetical simulation results.) In another plant-food experiment with random assignment, mean growth A minus B was 1.2 cm. In 200 re-randomizations, differences (A minus B) of 1.2 or more occurred 62 times. Decision rule: the model is the "no difference" model (plant food does not change growth). Count the simulated results that are differences of 1.2 or more (A minus B; a one-sided check). If they make up fewer than 5% of the simulated results, the model is not consistent with the data and the difference is significant; otherwise it is consistent and the difference is not significant. Which decision is correct?

choices.text: Not significant: re-randomizations can never be significant.
Significant: 62 is a large number of re-randomizations.
Not significant: chance gave such a difference 31% of the time.
Significant: the difference 1.2 is greater than 0.

questions.correct_answer: Not significant: chance gave such a difference 31% of the time.
